rationale: A wins because it finds the live wire without borrowing drama from outside the update: "Perplexity starts paying the publishers it's been fighting" is the real conflict, properly proof-gated. B has one sharp move in "Perplexity Says It's Sharing Revenue With Publishers. It Won't Say How Much.", but then it starts writing checks the facts cannot cash, especially "Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon."
gaps_in_A: Refusing "The publisher-payout angle: how much will publishers actually earn?" is too blunt; payout opacity can be the story if framed as accountability, not duplicated as a numbers piece.
"One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" is useful but softer than the first two; without actual economics, it risks becoming strategy-talk with better shoes.
gaps_in_B: "Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon" invents a competitive frame; the update gives no Google, Amazon, market-share, or performance comparison.
"for the first time, an AI search product is inserting itself into the transaction" is an unsupported first-of-kind claim.
"publishers and their legal teams will need to respond publicly" overstates the why-now; the update says legal threats existed, not that a response is required or imminent.
"publisher participation appears opt-in; content is cited regardless" presents inference as fact; the update does not explain opt-in terms or treatment of nonparticipants.
